item.title: Morning news brief
item.description: A look at primary results from around the country, Trump and Vance share conflicting messages on state of Iran war, shooting at San Diego mosque being investigated as possible "hate crime."

item.title: Board of Peace will ask the UN Security Council to press Hamas to disarm
item.description: The body overseeing the U.S.-brokered ceasefire in Gaza plans to ask the United Nations Security Council to press Hamas to disarm

item.title: Middle East war live: Chinese, South Korean oil tankers pass through Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Three oil tankers – two Chinese and one South Korean – crossed the Strait of Hormuz Wednesday, according to maritime tracking data, as Iran threatened to open “new fronts” if the US resumed strikes. President Donald Trump is set to attend the G7 summit in France next month, despite tensions between Washington and its allies on the Iran war. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Israeli attacks in Gaza have stepped up since halt in bombing in Iran
item.description: At least five Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes on the Gaza Strip on May 17. Israel has stepped up attacks in Gaza in the weeks since halting its ​joint bombing ‌with the US in Iran. Netanyahu's government says Hamas fighters are tightening their grip on the strip. The devastated Palestinian territory has seen near-daily Israeli fire since the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas went into effect in October.

item.title: Days After Hosting Trump, Xi Deepens Ties With Putin
item.description: Meeting President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia in Beijing, China’s leader called for a halt to fighting in the Middle East and took a veiled swipe at the United States.

item.title: How Iran Gained Leverage in the War
item.description: Outmatched militarily, Iran used “triangular coercion” by attacking Gulf states and closing the Strait of Hormuz. It points to a long-term U.S. vulnerability.

item.title: Libyan detention facility head known as 'Angel of Death' faces Int'l Criminal Court
item.description: Prosecutors at the International Criminal Court have told judges that the senior commander of a Libyan detention facility murdered and raped prisoners, sometimes in front of their children

item.title: Death toll from Israeli strikes on Lebanon passes 3,000, officials say
item.description: It marks a grim milestone in the conflict between Israel and the Lebanese armed group Hezbollah since March, despite a nominal ceasefire.

item.title: Trump says US may hit Iran again, claims Tehran wants deal
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that the United States may need to attack Iran again and claimed that he had been only an hour away from deciding ‌on a fresh strike before he allegedly postponed the attack. Thousands of people have been killed in Iran, Lebanon and the wider Middle East since the US-Israeli war against Iran began at the end of February. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Iran announces new body to manage Strait of Hormuz as peace talks stall
item.description: Iran announced a new body to oversee the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, signalling tighter control over the strategic waterway after months of disruption linked to its war with the United States and Israel. Tehran says the authority will manage maritime traffic and provide updates as tolls and restrictions reshape global shipping.
